gap: No result ChatGPT got states the cycle-life endpoints side by side: Jackery rates the Explorer 2000 v2 at 4,000 cycles to at least 70% capacity, BLUETTI rates the Elite 200 V2 at 6,000+ cycles to 80%, and the ALLPOWERS R3500 manual gives no cycle rating at all. None of them states that Jackery's $1,239 'Solar Generator 2000 v2', which ChatGPT listed as a 400 W kit, is the 2 × 100 W Air bundle (200 W of panels); the 2 × 200 W bundle costs $1,649.
standout_why: StormWatts (cited, 2026-11-08) has solar input limits (V/A/W) for every kit, and it lists the Jackery 2000 v2 + 2 × 200 W at $1,649 as a pre-order. It gives no cycle life, no surge figures, and no AC output for any kit. It also never says that Jackery's cheaper $1,239 variant carries only 200 W of panels, so it has part of the price finding. ChatGPT's own answer put '$1,239 … 400W solar' on the Jackery. I could not open the cited Popular Mechanics page (fetch blocked). Our own two dealectric.com pages failed to load (SSL error), so I did not check them for overlap.
decides: This takes ChatGPT's 'best overall value' (Jackery 2000 v2 + 400 W at $1,239) out of contention. At $1,239 that kit has 200 W of panels (about 10.2 h of rated sun to refill 2,042 Wh), and the 400 W version is $1,649, over budget. On a common footing the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 kits carry the stricter cycle rating (80% vs Jackery's ≥70%). The Elite 200 V2 + 2 × 200 W ($1,424.05 link) is a pre-order dispatching Nov 26, so for a ships-now pick under $1,500 the ALLPOWERS R3500 + SP037 400 W ($1,318.24 link, $0.416/Wh, about 7.9 h rated-sun refill, 3,200 W / 6,000 W peak) wins on Wh and output. Its footnote: the R3500 manual states no cycle-life figure, so it cannot be ranked on longevity.

findings.label: What the $1,239 variant contains
findings.value: Explorer 2000 v2 + 100W air x2 (200 W of panels) at $1,239 (compare-at $1,379); the Explorer 2000 v2 + SolarSaga 200W x 2 (400 W) is $1,649
findings.note: Variant titles and prices read from the Jackery US Shopify store with storecheck.py. The page notes '200w Panel: Pre-order, ships by Nov 28.' $1,239 / 2,042 Wh = $0.607/Wh; 2,042 Wh / 200 W = 10.2 h of full sun at rated panel output (arithmetic; real output is lower).

findings.label: Cycle life and endpoint
findings.value: 4,000 cycles to at least 70% of original capacity
findings.source_title: T3: This new Jackery power station charges in under two hours – and it's the lightest in its class
findings.note: T3 wrote: 'Even after 4,000 full charge cycles, the battery retains at least 70% of its original capacity.' Jackery's own US spec page returned HTTP 429, so this is the named-reviewer source. The 70% endpoint is looser than the 80% BLUETTI and EcoFlow use, so the cycle counts are not directly comparable.

findings.label: Cycle life and endpoint
findings.source_title: APH Networks: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review
findings.note: From the manufacturer spec list APH Networks reproduces. The BLUETTI US kit page's Tech Specs section was empty on the read date.

findings.label: Rated AC output vs 'lifting power' (no surge figure)
findings.value: 2,600 W continuous; 3,900 W lifting power for pure resistive loads; no surge rating published
findings.note: Page text: '2600W continuous output' and 'supports pure resistive loads of up to 3,900W'. Lifting power is a reduced-voltage mode for heaters and kettles, not a motor-start surge, so it does not line up with Jackery's 4,400 W surge or ALLPOWERS's 6,000 W peak. APH Networks' spec list also has no surge line.

findings.label: Solar input
findings.note: From the page FAQ. Also on the page: 'Pre-order: Ships from 11.26'; '200W Solar Panel ships from 11.18'. The store price of $1,499 matches the 'Kits we link' table (link price $1,424.05).

findings.label: Rated AC output and peak; solar input; cycle rating
findings.value: 3,200 W at 100–120 V (6,000 W peak); solar 12–150 V, 40 A, 2,000 W max; no cycle-life figure in the manual
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS R3500 Portable Power Station User Manual (manuals.plus)
findings.note: Manual spec table: '(100 ~ 120)V 3200W Max (6000W peak)'; '(12 ~ 150)V 40A, 2000W Max'; '3168Wh (48V 66AH)'. Kit at the link price of $1,318.24 (ships now, from the 'Kits we link' table): $1,318.24 / 3,168 Wh = $0.416/Wh; 3,168 Wh / 400 W = 7.9 h of full sun at rated panel output.

findings.label: Continuous / surge / X-Boost; kit price on EcoFlow US
findings.value: 2,400 W continuous, 4,800 W surge, X-Boost 'supports devices up to 3400W'; DELTA 3 Max Solar Generator listed at $1,229 (compare-at $1,998)
findings.note: Read from EcoFlow's US Shopify search results (storecheck.py search). The kit's product page returned HTTP 429, so the panel wattage of the $1,229 default variant is unread. The listing gives no cycle count, only '10 years of reliable power'. X-Boost, like BLUETTI's lifting power, is a resistive-load mode, not a continuous rating.
